The *Udapānadāyakattheraapadāna* is a Pali verse text preserved within the Therāpadāna collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya (numbered as Tha Ap 176) [SuttaCentral]. The title indicates an account of an elder whose past meritorious deed involved the gift of a well (*udapāna*). SuttaCentral records five modern translations of this biographical poem across five languages [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels have been identified in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan Buddhist corpora [DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates that the work shares conventional stock formulas with several other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, registering 13 matching passages across five distinct texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse occurs across verses §2.1–5.1, with close alignments found in the *Ekāsanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 254, §3.1–6.1), *Abbhañjanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 276, §5.1–7.1; Tha-Ap 526, §7.3–9.1), *Upāhanadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 258, §2.3–5.1), and *Mañcadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 360, §3.1–6.1) [DharmaNexus]. These shared verses reflect the standard structural phrasing used to narrate the karmic fruits of making material offerings to past Buddhas and their communities.
